final_answer: Its cytoplasmic tail binds ERM proteins (ezrin/radixin/moesin) and ankyrin, coupling extracellular HA binding to actin and to migration/signaling machinery.
note: Evidence PMC4423434 states the cytoplasmic tail binds ankyrin and ERM proteins (ezrin, radixin, moesin), and PMC5260879 states ERM proteins provide a link to the actin cytoskeleton.

final_answer: TSG-6 binds HA and catalyzes transfer of heavy chains from inter-alpha-inhibitor onto HA, forming HC-HA complexes that dampen neutrophil migration and inflammation.
note: Evidence PMC7749718 states TSG-6 catalyzes transfer of heavy chains from inter-alpha-trypsin inhibitor to HA forming HC-HA complexes, and PMC5807166 states TSG-6 can block chemotactic signals that induce neutrophil infiltration.

final_answer: Other GAGs (chondroitin sulfates, dermatan sulfate, heparin), plus acetylated LDL and other scavenger ligands - it is a broad clearance receptor, with HA its highest-turnover ligand.
note: Evidence PMC4839745 lists HARE/Stab2 clearance ligands including heparin, dermatan sulphate, chondroitin, chondroitin sulfate types A, C, D and E, and oxidized or acetylated LDL; PMC4276495 adds chondroitin sulfates and heparin.

final_answer: TLR2 and TLR4 (DAMP-like signaling to NF-kB). Caveat: effects are preparation- and purity-dependent, and endotoxin contamination confounded some early studies.
note: TLR2/TLR4 engagement is supported (PMC4045461), but no window supports the NF-kB claim or the stated caveat that effects are preparation-/purity-dependent and endotoxin contamination confounded early studies; the only contamination mention is avoiding LPS contamination of a HYAL preparation in one experiment.

final_answer: B - liver sinusoidal endothelial cells via HARE/Stabilin-2.
note: Evidence PMC7279005 states Stabilin-2 is highly expressed in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells and is responsible for the systemic clearance of HA, matching option B.

final_answer: About 85-90 kDa for the standard CD44 (sCD44).
note: Draft's 80-95 kDa range and ~37 kDa core figure are not in the evidence; PMC5339222 states: "The standard CD44 (sCD44) is the conserved form with a molecular weight of about 85–90 kDa".

final_answer: A hexasaccharide is about the minimum for detectable binding; stable, high-avidity binding needs longer chains (roughly decasaccharide and up, and in practice much longer/multivalent presentation).
note: No evidence window gives a minimum HA chain length (hexasaccharide) or a length required for high-affinity binding (decasaccharide and up); the windows discuss CD44-targeted aptamers and multivalent binding only.

final_answer: HMMR (hyaluronan-mediated motility receptor).
note: Evidence PMC7226759 states: "Hyaluronan mediated motility receptor (HMMR, also known as RHAMM)".

final_answer: HMW-HA multivalently clusters CD44 into assemblies that favor homeostatic/anti-inflammatory signaling, whereas short fragments bind without the same clustering and instead engage TLR2/4-type pro-inflammatory pathways - one basis of MW-dependent biology.
note: Evidence PMC3522304 states high and low molecular weight HA provoke distinct pro- and anti-inflammatory effects via CD44, long HA chains are multivalent while oligomers have one to two binding sites and reduced CD44 clustering; PMC6719336 states low-MW HA signaling involves TLR4 and TLR2.

final_answer: PI3K/Akt (survival) and Ras/MAPK-ERK (proliferation/migration), with additional links to Rho GTPases and EMT transcription programs.
note: Evidence PMC3403533 is titled "CD44 signaling via PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK pathways", and PMC5589713 states CD44s stimulates PI3K/Akt activation while CD44v augments MAPK signaling.

final_answer: Long HA strands crosslinked by TSG-6-catalyzed heavy-chain transfer (HC-HA cables) that form on stressed smooth-muscle/epithelial cells and capture monocytes/macrophages via CD44, organizing inflammatory cell adhesion.
note: No evidence window mentions HA cables, cable formation on stressed smooth-muscle/epithelial cells, or capture of monocytes/macrophages via CD44; the windows cover only TSG-6 heavy-chain transfer, osteoarthritis and wound healing.

final_answer: HAS2 acts in a ZEB1/ESRP1/HAS2/CD44 feedback circuit that drives epithelial-hybrid-mesenchymal transition: depleting HAS2 prevented the TGFbeta-induced epithelial-to-mesenchymal phenotype transition by about 50% and HAS2 knockdown inhibited cell migration - and in the TGFbeta model this role of HAS2 was independent of its hyaluronan-synthesizing activity.
note: Draft attributes the effect to HA production and Twist/Snail, which the evidence does not support; PMC3778714 states: "the role of HAS2 in TGFβ-mediated EMT is independent of its hyaluronan synthesizing activity" and that "depletion of HAS2 prevented the transition of the epithelial cobble-stone phenotype to spindle-like mesenchymal phenotype by about 50%".

final_answer: B - LYVE-1 is a CD44 homolog with a Link module, expressed on lymphatic endothelium.
note: Evidence PMC5122770 states LYVE-1 "was originally identified and characterized as a homologue of CD44" and a member of the Link module superfamily, matching option B.

final_answer: On resting cells the HA-binding site is masked (notably by sialylated glycans and receptor conformation); cytokine activation remodels glycosylation/clustering and unmasks binding, letting HA adhesion be switched on at inflammatory sites.
note: Evidence PMC7933184 states CD44-HA activation levels have been attributed to varying degrees of sialylation and that glycosylation-dependent affinities could stem from masking of high-affinity binding sites, with activation-dependent glycan remodeling.

final_answer: Hematopoietic and neural stem-cell niches (and MSC pericellular matrices): HMW-HA-rich coats support quiescence, self-renewal, and niche retention via CD44.
note: The windows mention CD44 as a stem-cell niche component, hematopoietic stem cell niches, and neural stem cell niche ECM, but none mention HA or HMW-HA coats, MSC pericellular matrices, or HA supporting quiescence/self-renewal/niche retention via CD44.

final_answer: Only a few minutes (about 2-5 minutes) due to rapid hepatic sinusoidal clearance.
note: No evidence window states a serum half-life for HA or any value in minutes, and none states rapid hepatic sinusoidal clearance; the windows discuss HA only as a hepatic fibrosis biomarker.

final_answer: It stabilizes the non-covalent binding of aggrecan's G1 domain to HA, locking the aggregate together.
note: Evidence PMC4648834 describes "The link protein (LP) that stabilizes the proteoglycan aggregate", whose A domain interacts with the aggrecan G1 region and B domains interact with HA; PMC3761224 states the IgV domain of HAPLN1 binds aggrecan whereas the link domains bind HA.

final_answer: It acts as a co-receptor for receptor tyrosine kinases such as c-Met (HGF receptor) and VEGFR-2, coupling CD44v6 to growth-factor signaling in cancer and angiogenesis.
note: Evidence PMC6328617 states CD44v6 "acts as a coreceptor for some growth factors", binds HGF and VEGF, and that MET phosphorylation falls when CD44v6 is absent in the presence of HGF.

final_answer: Ectodomain shedding (metalloproteinases) followed by gamma-secretase cleavage releases the CD44 intracellular domain (CD44-ICD), which translocates to the nucleus and influences transcription, including of CD44 itself.
note: Evidence PMC2172408 states ectodomain cleavage triggers intramembrane cleavage by presenilin-dependent gamma-secretase releasing CD44ICD, which translocates to the nucleus and activates gene transcription; PMC5339222 states the ICD activates transcription of proteins including CD44 itself.

final_answer: Inflamed endothelium displays HA (often as TSG-6-modified cables) that supports CD44-mediated rolling/adhesion of lymphocytes and monocytes, an auxiliary capture pathway alongside selectins.
note: Evidence supports CD44-HA supporting lymphocyte rolling and endothelial HA in T-cell recruitment, but does not establish TSG-6-modified cables, monocyte rolling (raised only as an open question in PMC13299323), or a pathway alongside selectins.
